tweets.text: That does seem like the rational expectation. But I think it’s still intriguing to consider the possibility it’s not true in this special case of making very personal connections. The profundity of such situations is that there is no closer medium to express or reveal your genuine self than your own words.  It’s worth contemplating the weight of that.  The issue goes way beyond writing.  How can anything be a truer expression of you than you? And if you see yourself as too flawed or mediocre to expose to other people directly, improving yourself may be a better remedy than hiding yourself.

tweets.text: I’ve always tried to respond to students who are excited about exploring something new.  I don’t always manage to do it, but that’s mainly just because of my email box getting overloaded.  With these new soulless emails I still in principle want to do it because I know someone is lost back there behind those words who does have something driving them, but I have to admit getting the enthusiasm together to do it is much harder.

tweets.text:
I wanted to share an experience about how difficult it is to automate “good writing” through LLMs. I’ve received many emails about AI from students over the years, going back long ago to around the time I shared source code for NEAT.  These communications are often endearing.  The joy of someone discovering a new frontier is a privilege to share. The “quality of writing” hardly matters - it’s the authenticity that is so compelling. 

But now, in the last year or so, I’ve noticed a switch in many of these kinds of emails.  Not all of them, but sometimes, they’re displays of polished genericism, like news releases about someone’s personal work, with words and phrases few young people would naturally choose. 

And that gives me a surprising feeling of sadness.  I can’t feel the person there anymore experiencing the rush of new ideas and possibilities.  I’ll still try to respond, and I am not trying to wage a crusade against assisted writing, but they don’t realize that their true power was their own authentic words, and this new shortcut they think they’ve found has taken that away from them. 

This scenario will not always be the case - sometimes we just want a generic clean exposition of a concept or idea.  But when you’re engaging in interpersonal communication (or even art), you’ll never find a tool beyond your own mind that makes you seem more like your authentic self.

quoted_tweet.text: I was curious why LLMs have gotten so good at math and still aren't that good at writing, so I asked an expert. It's not because math is easier. It's because it has clear right and wrong answers and so is easier to train on. But they are coming for me next.
